# The XOR path analysis:
# - edx starts at 0x5b (91)
# - For each position i: 
#   - input[i] XOR edx is compared against target[i]
#   - Then edx += input[i]
#
# So: target[i] = input[i] XOR edx
# Therefore: input[i] = target[i] XOR edx
# After getting input[i], update: edx = (edx + input[i]) & 0xFF (assuming single byte edx)

# Target bytes at 0x402050 (26 bytes for length 0x1a)
target = bytes.fromhex('1ded ac69 0e9d 38b0 5df9 680b a566 eb62 1896 33c9 72b8 f8cd'.replace(' ', ''))
print(f"Target bytes (26 expected): {len(target)} bytes")
print(f"Target hex: {target.hex()}")

target = bytes([0x1d, 0xed, 0xac, 0x69, 0x0e, 0x9d, 0x38, 0xb0, 0x5d, 0xf9, 
                0x68, 0x0b, 0xa5, 0x66, 0xeb, 0x62, 0x18, 0x96, 0x33, 0xc9,
                0x72, 0xb8, 0xf8, 0xcd, 0x1d, 0x20])

# Reverse the XOR
edx = 0x5b  # Initial value
result = []

    # input[i] = target[i] XOR (edx & 0xFF)
    input_byte = target[i] ^ (edx & 0xFF)
    result.append(input_byte)
    # edx is updated by adding input[i]
    edx = (edx + input_byte) & 0xFFFFFFFF  # Keep as 32-bit

recovered = bytes(result)
print(f"Recovered input: {recovered}")
print(f"Recovered as string: {recovered.decode('latin-1')}")

# Verify by running the forward transformation
edx = 0x5b
verified = []
for i in range(26):
    esi = edx ^ recovered[i]
    verified.append(esi & 0xFF)
    edx = (edx + recovered[i]) & 0xFFFFFFFF

print(f"Verification (should match target): {bytes(verified).hex()}")
print(f"Target was:                         {target.hex()}")
